<reason>Side A dismantled Side B's case by grounding the debate in the concrete unit economics and operational realities of peer-to-peer resale. Side A demonstrated that platforms already authenticate high-ticket luxury items where percentage commissions cover flat warehouse and labor costs, and proved that pushing physical hubs or relaxed buyer proof standards down into lower-priced everyday clothing either destroys affordability through fee hikes or invites buyer swap-and-return fraud. Side A also systematically exposed Side B's internal contradictions, such as dismissing photo verification in the opening only to rely on "photo forensics" in the second rebuttal.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>In [A4.3]-[A4.5], Side A dismantled Side B's pressure-question answers by showing that "tiering fees" concedes commission hikes on consumers, casual closet sellers cannot "batch shipments," and pivoting to "photo forensics" directly contradicted Side B's opening premise that counterfeiters cannot be caught with photos.</best_rebuttal>
